knowledge:
- key_parameters: object=The input Spectra, MsExperiment, or Chromatograms object containing mass spectrometry data ;; metrics=Character vector of quality metrics to calculate, defaults to qualityMetrics(object) ;; filterEmptyObject=Logical, if TRUE, removes zero-intensity, Inf-intensity, or zero-length entries prior to calculation ;; format=Character, either "data.frame" (default) or "mzQC" to export in rmzqc format ;; relativeTo=For ticQuartileToQuartileLogRatio, specifies baseline quantile ("Q1" or "previous") ;; msLevel=Integer, specifies the MS level (e.g., 1L, 2L) for filtering spectra
- alternatives: artMS=Uses MaxQuant output for QC metrics (correlation matrix, total intensity, peptide counts, charge state distribution) ;; MSstatsQC / MSstatsQCgui=Requires CSV files from Skyline/Panorama or MSnbase objects to generate control charts ;; MQmetrics=Proteomics/MaxQuant-specific metrics from MaxQuant files ;; MatrixQCvis=Interactive Shiny interface for rectangular matrices at various processing steps ;; proBatch=Focuses on batch effect assessment and correction in proteomics
- when_to_use: Appropriate for large-scale mass spectrometry experiments (e.g., clinical proteomics/metabolomics with thousands of samples) to track technical variation, shifts in data quality, and identify low-quality samples.
- pitfalls: Quality metrics only give an indication of quality and should not be used to blindly remove samples without further scrutiny (e.g., using MatrixQCvis) ;; Quality must always be evaluated in the context of sample type, experimental setup, and instrumentation (compare like-with-like) ;; Some metrics are specific to object types (e.g., scan-based metrics for Spectra, trace-based/peak-shape metrics for Chromatograms)

workflows.name: spectral_qc_spectra_msexperiment
workflows.intent: Calculate and visualize HUPO-PSI mzQC quality metrics from mass spectrometry spectral data using Spectra or MsExperiment objects.
input: fls (character vector of paths to mzML, mzXML, or CDF files)
workflows.stages: 1. Load libraries and register parallel backend ;; 2. Create a Spectra object from raw files ;; 3. Create an MsExperiment object to group samples and link sample metadata ;; 4. Retrieve available metrics using qualityMetrics() ;; 5. Calculate metrics using calculateMetrics() ;; 6. Visualize metrics using plotMetric() or explore interactively with shinyMsQuality()
workflows.code:
library("Spectra")
library("MsExperiment")
library("Chromatograms")
library("MsQuality")
library("BiocParallel")

register(SerialParam())

library(MsDataHub)
fls <- c(MsDataHub::X20171016_POOL_POS_1_105.134.mzML(),
         MsDataHub::X20171016_POOL_POS_3_105.134.mzML())
sps_sciex <- Spectra(fls, backend = MsBackendMzR())

lmse <- MsExperiment()
sd <- DataFrame(sample_id = c("QC1", "QC2"),
    sample_name = c("QC Pool", "QC Pool"),
    injection_idx = c(1, 3))
sampleData(lmse) <- sd
experimentFiles(lmse) <- MsExperimentFiles(mzML_files = fls)
spectra(lmse) <- sps_sciex
lmse <- linkSampleData(lmse, with = "experimentFiles.mzML_files",
    sampleIndex = c(1, 2), withIndex = c(1, 2))

data("Lee2019", package = "MsQuality")
sps_comb <- c(sps_rplc, sps_hilic)
sps_comb_subset <- sps_comb[grep("Sample.1_", sps_comb$dataOrigin), ]

metrics_sps_Q1 <- calculateMetrics(object = sps_comb_subset,
    metrics = qualityMetrics(sps_comb_subset), filterEmptyObject = FALSE,
    relativeTo = "Q1", msLevel = 1L)

msexp_rplc_subset <- msexp_rplc[1:20]
msexp_hilic_subset <- msexp_hilic[1:20]

metrics_rplc_msexp <- calculateMetrics(object = msexp_rplc_subset,
    metrics = qualityMetrics(msexp_rplc_subset), filterEmptyObject = TRUE,
    relativeTo = "Q1", msLevel = 1L)

metrics_hilic_msexp <- calculateMetrics(object = msexp_hilic_subset,
    metrics = qualityMetrics(msexp_hilic_subset), filterEmptyObject = TRUE,
    relativeTo = "Q1", msLevel = 1L)

metrics_msexp <- rbind(metrics_rplc_msexp, metrics_hilic_msexp)
plotMetric(qc = metrics_msexp, metric = "numberSpectra")
plotMetric(qc = metrics_msexp, metric = "ticQuartileToQuartileLogRatio")
shinyMsQuality(qc = metrics_msexp)

workflows.name: chromatographic_qc_chromatograms
workflows.intent: Calculate quality metrics from chromatographic traces and peak shapes using Chromatograms objects.
input: chromatographic_data.csv (manually defined or extracted chromatographic data containing retention times and intensities)
workflows.stages: 1. Load libraries ;; 2. Create a Chromatograms object ;; 3. Retrieve available metrics using qualityMetrics() ;; 4. Calculate metrics using calculateMetrics()
workflows.code:
library("Spectra")
library("MsExperiment")
library("Chromatograms")
library("MsQuality")
library("BiocParallel")

register(SerialParam())

cdata <- data.frame(
    msLevel = c(1L, 1L),
    mz = c(112.2, 123.3),
    dataOrigin = c("sample_1", "sample_1")
)
pdata <- list(
    data.frame(rtime = c(1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0),
               intensity = c(100, 250, 400, 300, 150)),
    data.frame(rtime = c(1.2, 1.8, 2.4, 3.0),
               intensity = c(50, 150, 300, 200))
)
chr <- Chromatograms(ChromBackendMemory(), chromData = cdata, peaksData = pdata)

metrics_chr <- calculateMetrics(object = chr, metrics = qualityMetrics(chr))
metrics_chr
